label: Research agents
title: Evidence systems and research agents
intro: These papers treat research as a sequence of search, reading, state management, verification, and stopping decisions. The business question is not whether an agent can produce a long report. It is whether the organization can inspect how the report acquired and tested its evidence.

papers.title: OpenResearcher
papers.contribution: Makes long research trajectories reproducible with a fixed corpus and explicit search, open, and find operations.
papers.business: Can a due-diligence run be replayed after a decision is challenged?

papers.title: OpenSeeker
papers.contribution: Builds difficult multi-hop questions from web structure and compresses noisy search history.
papers.business: Can training cases require real evidence traversal instead of keyword matching?

papers.title: DRACO
papers.contribution: Evaluates research reports across factual accuracy, coverage, presentation, and citation quality.
papers.business: Does the acceptance test score the dimensions the decision owner actually needs?

papers.title: DeepSearchQA
papers.contribution: Tests exhaustive, multi-step search where entity resolution and stopping are part of the task.
papers.business: Does the system stop because the answer set is complete or because its budget expired?

papers.title: DR Tulu
papers.contribution: Trains long-form research with rubrics that evolve as the policy discovers new evidence and failure modes.
papers.business: Can evaluation keep discriminating after the system learns yesterday's checklist?

papers.title: Tongyi DeepResearch
papers.contribution: Combines agentic mid-training, post-training, automatic data synthesis, and a compressed working memory.
papers.business: Which research state must remain verbatim, and which can be summarized safely?

papers.title: PokeeResearch
papers.contribution: Isolates reward, RL algorithm, data curation, and error recovery as separate design choices.
papers.business: Is a weak result caused by the model, the training signal, the task mix, or brittle execution?

papers.title: SFR-DeepResearch
papers.contribution: Shows a single agent can combine web search, page reading, and Python under a compact tool interface.
papers.business: Is a multi-agent organization necessary, or is it hiding a simpler control problem?

papers.title: DeepResearcher
papers.contribution: Trains research behavior against the noisy live web rather than only a closed retrieval corpus.
papers.business: Has the evaluation included blocked pages, stale snippets, and inconsistent sources?

papers.title: ReSearch
papers.contribution: Learns when to interleave reasoning and search without supervised reasoning traces.
papers.business: Does the agent search to resolve uncertainty, or merely because a workflow tells it to?

papers.title: Search-R1
papers.contribution: Uses outcome-based RL to teach multiple real-time searches inside a reasoning trajectory.
papers.business: Are search calls improving the answer enough to justify their latency and cost?

papers.title: Advancing Search Augmented Language Models
papers.contribution: Separates supervised deployment behavior from RL for accuracy and efficient tool use.
papers.business: Which requirements are hard guardrails, and which should be optimized from outcomes?

papers.title: Is Grep All You Need
papers.contribution: Finds that retrieval quality depends on the tool harness and presentation, not only the retrieval algorithm.
papers.business: Has the team compared the simplest exact-search baseline inside the actual user workflow?

label: Evaluation & safety
title: Evaluation, governance, and safety
intro: This cluster is about proxies. Benchmarks, rubrics, verifiers, safety classifiers, and privacy filters can make quality measurable, but every proxy creates a new surface for overfitting or omission.

papers.title: FRAMES
papers.contribution: Combines retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, and factual response quality in end-to-end RAG questions.
papers.business: Does a RAG test isolate retrieval failure from reasoning failure?

papers.title: CRAG
papers.contribution: Adds diverse question types and simulated web and knowledge-graph APIs to factual QA.
papers.business: Does the test set include changing facts, unavailable facts, and false premises?

papers.title: FanOutQA
papers.contribution: Measures broad answer-set construction with human decompositions across many documents.
papers.business: Can the system enumerate a market completely without duplicating the same entity?

papers.title: MultiHop-RAG
papers.contribution: Tests inference, comparison, temporal, and null questions that require several documents.
papers.business: Can the system say that no supported answer exists after a multi-source search?

papers.title: Artificial Hivemind
papers.contribution: Measures how model answers collapse diverse human preferences into similar responses.
papers.business: Is an ideation tool widening the option set or standardizing everyone on one safe answer?

papers.title: Unsupervised Process Reward Models
papers.contribution: Locates likely first errors in reasoning without step labels or final-answer verification.
papers.business: Can process monitoring find where a workflow first went wrong before damage propagates?

papers.title: Rubric Dropout
papers.contribution: Randomly hides rubric criteria during training so a policy cannot optimize one fixed checklist.
papers.business: Does performance survive when auditors vary the inspection criteria?

papers.title: Shieldstral
papers.contribution: Frames multimodal moderation under configurable policies as binary question answering.
papers.business: Can policy changes be versioned independently from the content classifier?

papers.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier
papers.contribution: Uses the verifier's score distribution instead of a single discrete judgment.
papers.business: Are borderline cases routed by calibrated uncertainty rather than a brittle pass or fail?

papers.title: Rubric Guided Self Distillation
papers.contribution: Distills rubric-conditioned behavior into a model that no longer needs a verifier on every call.
papers.business: Which quality controls can be internalized, and which still require independent review?

papers.title: POW3R
papers.contribution: Reweights rubric criteria according to which ones still distinguish current outputs.
papers.business: Is optimization effort spent on unresolved quality gaps rather than already-saturated metrics?

papers.title: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL
papers.contribution: Shows that better rubric scores can coexist with worse broader quality.
papers.business: What holdout review would reveal checklist compliance without actual improvement?

papers.title: IFBench
papers.contribution: Tests instruction following on new, programmatically verifiable constraints.
papers.business: Does a workflow obey unfamiliar contractual formats or only templates seen in tuning?

papers.title: OpenAI Privacy Filter
papers.contribution: Uses an efficient long-context token classifier to find and redact personal information.
papers.business: Is privacy filtering measured for recall, over-redaction, context length, and local policy?

papers.title: How2Everything
papers.contribution: Builds data, a benchmark, and a judge for detecting critical errors in generated procedures.
papers.business: Can an operations assistant be tested for unsafe omissions rather than fluent wording?

papers.title: Likelihood-Based Reward Designs
papers.contribution: Compares probability and log-probability rewards across verifiable and open-ended reasoning.
papers.business: Does the reward preserve meaningful differences, or collapse outcomes into a coarse binary signal?

papers.title: IH Challenge
papers.contribution: Trains and evaluates obedience to instruction priority across system, developer, user, and tool roles.
papers.business: Can lower-trust content override policy or authorization in the deployed prompt stack?

papers.title: Rubrics as Rewards
papers.contribution: Turns instance-specific, interpretable criteria into reinforcement-learning rewards.
papers.business: Can domain experts inspect and amend the definition of a good result?

label: Training & adaptation
title: Training, curricula, and specialist agents
intro: The common theme is allocation: which examples, traces, rewards, teachers, and specialist tasks deserve training compute. For a business, the practical unit is not the parameter count alone but the cost of acquiring a dependable capability.

papers.title: Nemotron Labs IMO 2026
papers.contribution: Uses repeated natural-language proof generation, verification, and refinement without a formal prover.
papers.business: When does an expensive generate-check-refine loop beat one fast answer?

papers.title: GenCluster
papers.contribution: Clusters diverse candidate programs before ranking and submission.
papers.business: Can validation spend cover different solution families instead of near-duplicates?

papers.title: Nemotron 3 CC
papers.contribution: Joins problem curation, synthetic traces, SFT, RL, and test-time correction for competitive programming.
papers.business: Which stage contributes measurable reliability in an agentic software pipeline?

papers.title: Complete Reasoning Traces
papers.contribution: Finds that partial or endpoint traces can retain much of the post-training value of full traces.
papers.business: Are costly full process logs necessary, or would verified milestones carry the signal?

papers.title: SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists
papers.contribution: Reports stronger cross-task interference in sequential SFT than in sparse RL updates.
papers.business: Does adding one capability erase another in the release regression suite?

papers.title: Is One Layer Enough
papers.contribution: Concentrates much of the measured RL gain in a small number of middle layers.
papers.business: Can adaptation scope be narrowed without losing the target behavior?

papers.title: TailSFT
papers.contribution: Focuses SFT on sequences the model has not yet covered rather than repeatedly fitting easy cases.
papers.business: Is the training queue reducing failure coverage or only average loss?

papers.title: TinyGSM
papers.contribution: Uses large synthetic math data plus a verifier to train small generation systems.
papers.business: Can synthetic cases and automated checks substitute for scarce expert-written examples?

papers.title: TinyStories
papers.contribution: Constrains vocabulary and story structure so very small models expose learning behavior clearly.
papers.business: Can a reduced-domain prototype test the learning pipeline before full-scale spend?

papers.title: CLRS-Text
papers.contribution: Expresses algorithmic execution traces as text across classical tasks.
papers.business: Can process reasoning be evaluated against exact state transitions rather than prose quality?

papers.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
papers.contribution: Combines token-level teacher guidance with trajectory-level correctness.
papers.business: Can dense coaching remain subordinate to the outcome that matters?

papers.title: Passive Skill Distillation
papers.contribution: Extracts reusable procedural skills from agent trajectories and injects them as compact instructions.
papers.business: Which repeated workflow knowledge belongs in a playbook instead of the model weights?

papers.title: SOAR
papers.contribution: Rewards a problem-generating teacher according to the student's improvement on hard cases.
papers.business: Can test generation be optimized for learning value rather than novelty alone?

papers.title: SCRL
papers.contribution: Converts hard problems into verified subproblems ordered as a curriculum.
papers.business: Can a complex business process be taught through auditable intermediate competencies?

papers.title: Compress Distil
papers.contribution: Rewrites long correct reasoning traces into shorter supervision before training a student.
papers.business: How much explanation cost can be removed without removing the decision signal?

papers.title: Leanstral
papers.contribution: Specializes general code agents for Lean proof work without a bespoke operating shell.
papers.business: When should a shared agent interface host a high-assurance specialist?

papers.title: Unsupervised On-Policy Self Distillation
papers.contribution: Uses agreement among a model's own rollouts to create a corrective teaching signal.
papers.business: Can internal consensus improve a system without hiding correlated mistakes?

papers.title: TREK
papers.contribution: Uses a short teacher-guided phase to expand the student's exploration before returning to RL.
papers.business: Is a weak learner missing knowledge, or merely failing to visit useful solution modes?

papers.title: Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Teaches from demonstrations through a privileged self-teacher while the student trains on its own rollouts.
papers.business: Can new procedures be learned without a separate reward service or broad capability loss?

papers.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner
papers.contribution: Gives one model privileged answer information in the teacher role and removes it in the student role.
papers.business: What information may guide training but will not exist at production time?

papers.title: Generalized Knowledge Distillation
papers.contribution: Applies teacher feedback to sequences sampled from the student rather than only fixed teacher outputs.
papers.business: Is the teacher correcting mistakes the deployed student actually makes?

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation
papers.contribution: Constructs a capability direction from contrasting weak models and transfers it to a stronger student.
papers.business: Can cheap specialist signals improve a stronger general system without copying a weak model wholesale?

papers.title: OpenThoughts Agent
papers.contribution: Uses controlled ablations to identify which instructions, teachers, filters, and task sources matter for agent data.
papers.business: Has the data pipeline measured contribution by source rather than assuming more traces are better?

papers.title: VibeThinker-3B
papers.contribution: Combines curriculum SFT, multi-domain RL, and self-distillation in a compact reasoning model.
papers.business: What capability floor is achievable under a strict deployment-size budget?

papers.title: VibeThinker-1.5B
papers.contribution: Separates diverse solution discovery in SFT from reinforcement of correct paths in RL.
papers.business: Should exploration and reliability be optimized in different training stages?

papers.title: MAI-Thinking-1
papers.contribution: Builds a large reasoning model with human-generated data and iterative empirical optimization.
papers.business: Is model provenance compatible with the organization's licensing and audit requirements?

papers.title: Aryabhata 2
papers.contribution: Applies phased RL to a cleaned curriculum for competitive-exam reasoning.
papers.business: Does a narrow expert model benefit from domain sequencing more than a mixed training pool?

papers.title: Apriel-1.5-OpenReasoner
papers.contribution: Balances five reasoning domains with adaptive sampling and difficulty-aware length penalties.
papers.business: Can the training scheduler prevent one high-volume domain from consuming the model?

papers.title: Composer 2
papers.contribution: Trains a coding agent in realistic software environments for long planning and multi-step execution.
papers.business: Does coding evaluation include repository navigation, recovery, and end-to-end task completion?

papers.title: Beyond Web
papers.contribution: Rephrases targeted documents to make synthetic pretraining data denser and more diverse.
papers.business: Is synthetic data adding useful coverage or merely restating the same source distribution?

papers.title: The Art of Asking
papers.contribution: Optimizes translated prompts for naturalness, cultural fit, and difficulty across languages.
papers.business: Has a multilingual product localized the task itself, not only translated its words?

papers.title: Nemotron Cascade 2
papers.contribution: Combines multi-stage RL and on-policy distillation in an efficient mixture-of-experts model.
papers.business: Which staged training costs buy reusable capability across math, code, and agents?

papers.title: QED Nano
papers.contribution: Trains a compact proof model with SFT, rubric rewards, and an iterative reasoning cache.
papers.business: Can formal-quality output be decomposed into drafting, checking, and memory controls?

label: Architecture & efficiency
title: Architecture, context, and deployment efficiency
intro: These papers change where computation and parameters live. Their business relevance is a cost ledger: training cost, serving cost, task-specific storage, latency, and operational flexibility are different quantities.

papers.title: NoRA
papers.contribution: Normalizes LoRA's down-projection to improve optimization while retaining exact mergeability.
papers.business: Does a cheaper adaptation method remain stable across tasks and release merges?

papers.title: Low-Rank Training
papers.contribution: Applies low-rank parameterization to feed-forward layers during pretraining, not only adaptation.
papers.business: Is the organization reducing training compute or only task-specific parameter count?

papers.title: YaRN
papers.contribution: Extends RoPE context lengths with limited additional training.
papers.business: Does the long-context claim survive the document lengths and positions in production?

papers.title: NoPE
papers.contribution: Challenges explicit positional encodings on length generalization tasks.
papers.business: Is the architecture feature improving the target workload or persisting by convention?

papers.title: ALiBi
papers.contribution: Adds distance-dependent attention bias instead of positional embeddings.
papers.business: Can longer inputs be supported without retraining the entire representation scheme?

papers.title: RoPE
papers.contribution: Represents absolute position through rotation while exposing relative distance in attention.
papers.business: Which context-extension methods remain compatible with the deployed backbone?

papers.title: Position Encodings
papers.contribution: Compares the mechanisms that give a parallel Transformer token order.
papers.business: Is sequence order encoded in a way that matches extrapolation and latency requirements?

papers.title: Kimi K3
papers.contribution: Combines sparse activation, native multimodality, and very long context at large scale.
papers.business: Which claimed capability requires the full model, and which can be served by a smaller route?

papers.title: Kimi K2.5
papers.contribution: Jointly trains text and vision for an open multimodal agentic model.
papers.business: Does multimodality improve the actual workflow or add an expensive unused interface?

papers.title: Sparse Upcycling
papers.contribution: Converts a trained dense checkpoint into a sparse mixture-of-experts model.
papers.business: Can sunk pretraining cost be reused without multiplying serving complexity?

papers.title: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni
papers.contribution: Adds native audio, image, and video support to an efficient sparse backbone.
papers.business: Which modalities need one shared model, and which require separate quality controls?

papers.title: Mellum 2
papers.contribution: Uses sparse experts for code editing, debugging, tool use, and conversational programming.
papers.business: Does one coding model meet both interactive latency and agentic execution needs?

papers.title: Mellum
papers.contribution: Targets low-latency, multi-line IDE completion with a compact open model.
papers.business: Is the product optimizing for completion speed rather than benchmark breadth?

papers.title: EMO
papers.contribution: Encourages domain-specialized experts that can be composed or deployed selectively.
papers.business: Can unused capabilities be removed from a deployment without retraining the whole model?

papers.title: Olmo 3
papers.contribution: Releases models, data, training details, and checkpoints across general and reasoning variants.
papers.business: Does openness reduce vendor risk enough to offset self-hosting responsibility?

papers.title: Arcee Trinity
papers.contribution: Mixes local and global attention with sparse experts and explicit load balancing.
papers.business: Are throughput gains preserved under the organization's real request distribution?

papers.title: Sarvam 30B and 105B
papers.contribution: Builds Indic-focused reasoning models with locally optimized tokenization.
papers.business: Does regional language coverage require a different tokenizer and data supply chain?

papers.title: Nemotron 3 Super
papers.contribution: Combines hybrid sequence layers, sparse experts, low precision, and multi-token prediction.
papers.business: Which optimization lowers total serving cost after hardware and software constraints are included?

label: Data & retrieval
title: Data and representation
intro: This group concerns what the system stores, compares, and retrieves. The practical concern is whether the representation preserves the distinctions needed by a search, classification, or multimodal workflow.

papers.title: Gemini Embedding 2
papers.contribution: Maps text, image, video, audio, and PDFs into one multilingual space with variable dimensions.
papers.business: Does one index improve cross-modal discovery without erasing modality-specific evidence?

papers.title: Jina Embeddings v5 Omni
papers.contribution: Adds frozen modality encoders around a text embedding space and trains small connectors.
papers.business: Can new document types be added without rebuilding the entire retrieval stack?

papers.title: gzip and Scaling Laws
papers.contribution: Uses compression as a proxy for data complexity when predicting scaling behavior.
papers.business: Can a cheap complexity measure improve data and compute planning before a training run?

papers.title: Text Classification with Gzip
papers.contribution: Combines normalized compression distance with nearest-neighbor classification.
papers.business: Has the team tested a transparent non-neural baseline before adopting a larger classifier?

papers.title: FinePhrase
papers.contribution: Treats synthetic pretraining data as a recipe optimized through many controlled experiments.
papers.business: Are synthetic-data costs tied to ablations that show which transformations help?

papers.title: Jina Embeddings v5 Text
papers.contribution: Combines distillation and contrastive objectives for compact, multilingual, quantization-tolerant embeddings.
papers.business: Do retrieval tests include truncation, language mix, and the quantized production index?
